author: template-projects
name: Aspire starter add-on: React front end
description: Adds a Vite + React 19 + TanStack + Tailwind front end to a scaffold created with aspire-base. Installable as a PWA. Emits .scaffold/aspire-ui-react.wiring.md, which lists the AppHost edits the scaffolding skill applies.

resource.description: The singular PascalCase name of the sample resource, e.g. Product. The scaffold's entity, controller, page and tests are named from it. The plural is this plus "s" - an irregular plural is a rename after scaffolding, not a second parameter. Pass the SAME value to every template in a scaffold, exactly like -n.

resourceLower.//: The lowercase form, for TypeScript identifiers, route paths and file names. A separate symbol because `replaces` is a literal substitution - unlike sourceName, it does not match case variants.

nameBlazorProject.//: This template's sourceName is the lowercase `template` and the engine matches it case-sensitively, so the PascalCase `Template.Blazor.*` project names that docs/DESIGN.md and index.css use to point at the Blazor half are not substituted by it. A React scaffold has no Blazor project, but those references still name the counterpart this design system is kept in step with, and a stale `Template.` prefix names something that never existed. Two details are load-bearing: the match is scoped to `Template.Blazor` rather than the bare word, because `Template` alone would also rewrite unrelated PascalCase uses; and the value has to carry the `.Blazor` suffix, because `replaces` swaps the whole matched string for it - a bare name would collapse `Template.Blazor.Maui.Pages` to `<Name>.Maui.Pages`.

modifiers.comment: package-lock.json names @babel/template and @babel/plugin-transform-template-literals. sourceName substitution would rewrite those package names and break npm install, so the file is copied byte for byte.
